method: Computed SHA-256 hashes and byte sizes for all three supplied PDFs and compared them against every evidence catalog.
Opened and text-extracted all 150 pages: 147 pages contain embedded text and three image-only EPA archive covers were visually verified as nonblank.
Rendered all 150 pages at 96 DPI, reviewed nine sequence-preserving contact sheets and inspected each Cadillac-specific page at full resolution.
Confirmed two supplied files are byte-for-byte matches to established catalog records and suppressed duplicate catalog entries.
Localized the two previously remote canonical records and retained the distinct January–March 2015 report so public users can preview and download without a GitHub account.
Separated the later 2014 carry-forward status from the distinct 2015 effluent-violation entries and preserved the evidentiary limits shown in the reports.

addedRecord.canonicalName: 2015-01-01 to 2015-03-31 - EPA ICIS Michigan Quarterly Non-Compliance Report.pdf

verifiedFindings: The January–March 2014 report's Cadillac row records an outfall 001 DMR overdue to EPA/State, underlying violation date December 31, 2013, status date February 20, 2014 and code 2D reporting violation.
The April–June 2014 report carries the same December 31, 2013 DMR reporting violation forward as continuing noncompliance in its September 13, 2014 data run; it is not a new violation entry.

The January–March 2015 report lists seven code 3A1 non-monthly-average permit-effluent violations for total ammonia as nitrogen and carbonaceous BOD at outfall 001-A, with violation dates from October 31, 2014 through March 31, 2015.
The displayed Cadillac rows show no linked enforcement action or final order.
evidentiaryBoundary: The reports are EPA ICIS quarterly status records. The relevant rows do not supply measured concentrations, loads, root-cause findings, PFAS results or independent proof of offsite impact. The 2014 entries concern one carried-forward reporting violation; the 2015 entries are separately identified permit-effluent violations.

queueResolution.reason: The reports add federal compliance-status evidence but do not supply the receiving-history, PFAS time series, complete receptor work order, certified well construction, water-level, hydraulic-test or source-to-receptor evidence requested by the remaining queue.
